All gates pass. Here's my report.

**STATUS: DONE**

**What I implemented** (`crates/bridge-acp/src/acp_backend.rs`, Task 5 of the slice-7b watchdog plan):

1. **TDD — 3 failing tests first** (verified `watchdog_cancels_a_hung_turn_as_timed_out` failed pre-implementation with `Elapsed`; the other two passed trivially since nothing existed yet to trip):
   - `watchdog_cancels_a_hung_turn_as_timed_out` — fake agent accepts prompt, never responds/emits; `hard_wall_clock=50ms`, `idle=10s` → stream's terminal item is `Err(BridgeError::AgentTimedOut)`.
   - `watchdog_does_not_trip_active_or_unmodeled_turn` — (a) Text chunks every 20ms then Done (`idle=100ms`, `wall=10s`) completes; (b) FIX-11: ONLY unmodeled `Thought` chunks every 20ms then Done also completes (proves the handler's unconditional bump keeps a dropped-event turn "alive").
   - `no_watchdog_config_is_byte_identical` — `watchdog: None` → a hung turn stays hung (no spurious timeout) within a 300ms bound.
   - Extended the `Recorder` test harness with `update_delay`/`set_update_delay` so scripted updates can drip over real wall-clock time (needed for the periodic-emission tests; didn't exist before).

2. **Implementation** in `prompt_inner`:
   - Setup: `watchdog_fired: Option<Arc<Notify>>` (mirrors `watch`'s `is_some()`), and — only when `watch`+config both present — a `oneshot` `(done_tx, done_rx)` plus a spawned `'static` watchdog task capturing `Arc<TurnWatch>`, the `Notify`, and the two `Duration`s. It loops: derive `deadline = min(wall_deadline, idle_deadline)` (idle only when `la != 0`, using the `la_instant = turn_start + Duration::from_millis(la.saturating_sub(1))` round-trip, PFIX-L), `select!{ sleep_until(Instant::from_std(deadline)) vs &mut done_rx }`, and on wake re-checks both bounds with saturating math (FIX-5) before `notify_one()`+return.
   - Driver `select!` gained a `_ = async { match &watchdog_fired { Some(n)=>n.notified().await, None=>pending().await } }` arm (PFIX-G: `Pending` when disabled) that runs the same bounded cancel (`CancelNotification` → inner `select!{ prompt_fut | kill | sleep(grace)→escalate_terminate }`) but **unconditionally** sets `timed_out_local = true; Err(())`, discarding the inner result (PFIX-F).
   - Teardown: `drop(watchdog_done_tx)` added right after `map.remove`/kill-slot clear, on every exit path.
   - Terminal: `Err(()) if timed_out_local => AgentTimedOut`, else the existing `AgentCrashed` path; `Ok(resp)` untouched (never relabeled).

**Tests:** `cargo test -p bridge-acp --lib` → 108 passed, 0 failed (includes the 3 new + all existing turn/cancel tests unchanged). `cargo test --workspace --no-run` → compiles clean. `cargo fmt --all --check` → clean (fmt was applied once). `cargo clippy -p bridge-acp --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. No flakes observed.

**Files changed:** only `crates/bridge-acp/src/acp_backend.rs` (+277/-5). Nothing committed, per instructions.

**Self-review vs the PFIX checklist:** watchdog arm always yields `Err(())`+`timed_out_local` regardless of inner outcome (confirmed no `Ok` leak); disabled path is genuinely `Pending` with no task spawned (guarded by one `if let (Some,Some,Some)`); `tokio::time::Instant::from_std` used for `sleep_until`; `la_instant` round-trip + saturating math present in both the deadline-derivation and the wake-recheck; `drop(watchdog_done_tx)` runs unconditionally on every exit; a natural `Ok(resp)` never touches `timed_out_local`; the inner `&mut prompt_fut` reborrow in the new arm's body is safe for the same reason it already is in the pre-existing `done_sender.closed()` arm (the outer select's other arm futures are dropped before a winning arm's body runs). No concerns to flag.
